annotation.title_clean: Robots in the moral loop: a field study of AI advisors in ethical military decision-making
annotation.title_en: Robots in the moral loop: a field study of AI advisors in ethical military decision-making
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Tossell, C.C.; Kuennen, C.; Momen, A.; Funke, G.; Tolston, M.; De Visser, E.J.
annotation.summary_en: Field study over three months with 62 US military cadets teamed with a humanoid robot or human moral advisor (SIEMA). Advice shifted graded moral judgments about soldier versus civilian lives about equally for robot and human advisors; later opposing advice often reversed shifts. Recommends transparent trade-off presentation and human reflection in moral-AI design.
key_provisions_or_claims: About half of cadets shifted toward the utilitarian option after advice, regardless of robot or human source.
Most shifted back after an opposing civilian-protection recommendation.
Explicit blind compliance was rare (under 8%) and did not differ by advisor type.
Moral-AI design should present trade-offs transparently and surface competing values concurrently.
Human reflection is needed rather than assuming isolated AI prompts durably reset moral priorities.
